clue.text: Russian composer reportedly suggests Mr Fleming should try a holiday trip

indicators.note: reportedly says the advice to Ian Fleming is to be heard spoken rather than read as written

parts.words: Mr Fleming should try a holiday trip
parts.note: Mr Fleming is Ian, and trying a holiday trip is to catch a tour: 'catch a tour, Ian'

explanation.surface: A Russian composer's name is heard as travel advice for the creator of James Bond.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'catch a tour, Ian' gives the composer's surname; Ian Fleming wrote the James Bond novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Aram Khachaturian was the Soviet Armenian composer of the ballets Spartacus and Gayane.

parts.note: a one-act play by Samuel Beckett in which an old man listens to a reel-to-reel recording of his younger self

explanation.definitionFit: The play's title names the spool of recorded diary that its hero replays on his birthday.

clue.text: Mathematician's little girl is a student with dessert

parts.note: L for learner, the plate worn by a student driver
ice, as in an ice cream or water ice served as a sweet course

explanation.surface: A mathematician's young daughter is at college and fond of pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: The mathematician is Charles Dodgson, Lewis Carroll, whose child heroine was modelled on Alice Liddell.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll, a mathematics don at Oxford, wrote his Wonderland books for the little Liddell girl of that name.

clue.text: Henry Blake Fuller's was concerned with hypostases, perhaps

definitions.text: Henry Blake Fuller's was concerned with hypostases, perhaps

parts.words: Henry Blake Fuller's was concerned with hypostases, perhaps
parts.note: points to the American novelist's book The ___ of La Trinité, whose title figure is a lady presiding over a castle

explanation.definitionFit: Fuller's 1892 novel is titled after the mistress of a château in an Alpine setting.

parts.note: a song that is short and light, a diminutive of the operatic aria

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the Italian diminutive of aria, a brief tuneful air.

parts.note: 'Dear Me' looks like an exclamation but is the title of the memoir by the actor and writer Sir Peter

explanation.definitionFit: Peter's 1977 memoir was called Dear Me, so the clue's exclamation is his book's title.

clue.text: Child's play for many a Deighton protagonist

explanation.surface: Spy fiction is dismissed as a game for children.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a guessing game for children in which one player names something seen; Len Deighton's narrators could say 'I am a spy' of themselves.

clue.text: One of those not known by Sir Charles Roberts?

definitions.text: One of those not known by Sir Charles Roberts?

parts.words: One of those not known by Sir Charles Roberts?
parts.note: refers to the Canadian writer's animal story collection The ___s Unknown, so one of the unknowns in his title

explanation.definitionFit: Charles G. D. Roberts called his 1910 book of wild-animal tales after the creatures living near us whom we never meet.

parts.note: a crotchet is a musical note of one beat
the castle is a chess piece, also called the rook

explanation.surface: A chess player called Note is apparently the work of someone named Peacock.
explanation.walkthrough: Peacock is Thomas Love Peacock, whose satirical novel of 1831 bears this name; 'by Peacock' defines a work of his.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Love Peacock's comic novel of talk at a country house is titled with this name.

clue.text: Writer like Orwell or Philip Barry? Or those featuring 19 and 23?

definitions.text: Writer like Orwell or Philip Barry? Or those featuring 19 and 23?

parts.words: Writer like Orwell or Philip Barry? Or those featuring 19 and 23?
parts.note: Orwell wrote Animal Farm and Barry the play The Animal Kingdom; a hummingbird and a wolf are subjects for an artist of beasts

explanation.definitionFit: An artist or writer who takes creatures as subject is so called, and both authors used beasts in a title.

explanation.surface: An earlier English poet is being described.
explanation.definitionFit: It means earlier in time, and Matthew Prior was an English poet and diplomat of around 1700.

clue.text: Quiet wife of Hercules is a shepherdess

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction to play softly
Hebe, goddess of youth, was married to Hercules after he became a god

explanation.surface: The hero's silent spouse turns out to tend sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: The shepherdess is the scornful one in Shakespeare's As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: In As You Like It, she is the country girl loved by Silvius who falls for Rosalind in disguise.

clue.text: Next book by Durrell, with never a sequel

definitions.text: Next book by Durrell, with never a sequel

parts.words: Next book by Durrell, with never a sequel
parts.note: Lawrence Durrell's novel has a Latin title meaning 'then', and its sequel was Nunquam, Latin for 'never'

explanation.definitionFit: Durrell's 1968 novel carries the Latin word for 'then'; its companion volume Nunquam means 'never'.

parts.note: a blind attempt is 'a ___ in the dark', the title of a novel by David Garnett

explanation.definitionFit: Garnett's 1958 novel A ___ in the Dark is named for an attempt made blindly.

indicators.note: something modified has been altered, so the letters of the two following words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Victorian is described as altered or improved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modified' rearranges OR and ENHANCED into a Tennyson title; 'Victorian' stands for that Victorian poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's 1864 narrative poem of a sailor returning to find his wife remarried is a classic Victorian work.

indicators.note: in places the article within the word for the particle

parts.note: the lambda is a subatomic particle named after the Greek letter
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a dance made of a small piece of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A into LAMBDA after its B.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazilian partner dance with close hip movement, a craze of 1989.

parts.note: a poet who works in archetypes and myths, as in myth-making verse

explanation.definitionFit: A maker of myths in poetry, one whose verse deals in primal archetypes.

clue.text: Transport giant to hotel for Dutch painter

parts.note: a van is a vehicle for transport
Gog is a giant of legend, paired with Magog in London's Guildhall
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Moving a huge figure to a hotel makes way for a Dutch painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincent, the post-impressionist of Sunflowers, was a Netherlands-born artist.

clue.text: Bertrand Russell wrote of such a presence in suburbia

definitions.text: Bertrand Russell wrote of such a presence in suburbia

parts.words: Bertrand Russell wrote of such a presence in suburbia
parts.note: Russell's story collection is titled Satan in the Suburbs, so the presence is a devilish one

explanation.definitionFit: A presence belonging to the devil, as in Russell's book of stories about the Prince of Darkness in suburbs.

clue.text: Kingsley's "living gem which hung, loud humming, over some fantastic bloom"

definitions.text: Kingsley's "living gem which hung, loud humming, over some fantastic bloom"

parts.words: Kingsley's "living gem which hung, loud humming, over some fantastic bloom"
parts.note: Charles Kingsley's description of a tiny bright bird that hovers and hums at flowers

explanation.definitionFit: It is a French word for a hummingbird, the jewel-like bird hovering at blossoms.

explanation.surface: A cutting is described as a passage.
explanation.definitionFit: A press cutting is an extract, and a passage quoted from a book is the same thing.

indicators.note: men who are led astray go off their proper course, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A group of men in fur coats is led off course by someone called Reid.
explanation.definitionFit: Trimmed with the white winter fur of the stoat, as robes of peers and judges are.

explanation.surface: Someone asks the weight of an old realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy weight is the system for weighing precious metals, and the city of Priam was besieged by the Greeks.

clue.text: Ancient kingdom where sex makes a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means the word for the sex is read from end to start

parts.note: male is one of the two sexes

explanation.surface: An old realm where sex returns to fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: This was an early state in what is now south-west Iran, with Susa as capital.

indicators.note: from signals the letters are taken out of the run of the place name

explanation.surface: A solitary wolf comes from a big Russian lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the letters running across 'lAKE LAdoga'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Kipling's Jungle Book, the leader of the Seeonee pack is called the Lone Wolf.

clue.text: Some of his output enigmatic? Variable?

definitions.text: Some of his output enigmatic? Variable?

parts.words: Some of his output enigmatic? Variable?
parts.note: points to the Enigma Variations, the orchestral work by an English composer

explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward composed the Enigma Variations of 1899, whose theme is a puzzle.

parts.note: Venerable is the title of the Anglo-Saxon historian, and Adam is George Eliot's hero of that surname

explanation.definitionFit: The Northumbrian monk-historian is called the Venerable, and George Eliot's carpenter hero is Adam of that name.

parts.note: Rushdie's famous verses are in fact in a novel, so not in poetry

explanation.definitionFit: Writing not in metre is the opposite of verse, and Rushdie's book of 'verses' is a novel.

clue.text: "Nor can in books be read: / The legend of a life more ——' " (Longfellow)

definitions.text: "Nor can in books be read: / The legend of a life more ——' " (Longfellow)

parts.words: "Nor can in books be read: / The legend of a life more ——' " (Longfellow)
parts.note: the missing word from Longfellow's lines, an archaic word for blessed

explanation.definitionFit: Longfellow's archaic adjective means blessed or favoured, completing the line about a holy life.

parts.note: J. B. Priestley's 1947 play is named for a lime tree, the linden being another name for it

explanation.definitionFit: Linden is another name for the lime tree, and Priestley's play bears that title.
